Perform a variable-cell relaxation (vc-relax) followed by an SCF total-energy calculation for BiFeO3, case vc_relax_scf__ferroelectric__8__bifeo3.
Use the local LDA pseudopotentials PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard/bi.upf, fe.upf, and o.upf.
Set etot_conv_thr = 1.0e-8, forc_conv_thr = 1.0e-7, and conv_thr = 1.0e-8.
Use an automatic Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid with a half shift in both runs.
Choose the ecutwfc cutoff and k-point mesh density yourself, selecting values appropriate for a converged LDA calculation on BiFeO3, and keep them consistent between the vc-relax and the SCF.
Use nonmagnetic (spin-unpolarized) settings with default (fixed) occupations in both runs, since no magnetic configuration is specified; report this choice in the results.
Obtain the starting structure by retrieving a primitive R3c BiFeO3 structure consistent with the metadata (formula BiFeO3, perovskite, space group R3c, 10 atoms per primitive cell) from a structure database, ensuring the rhombohedral distortion and atomic displacements of R3c are present.
If no structure-retrieval tool is available and no structure can be constructed from reliable R3c reference data, report that the local inputs lack sufficient structure data rather than using an incorrect starting cell.
Do not use an idealized cubic 5-atom perovskite cell as the starting structure.
Run the vc-relax to fully relax both the cell parameters and atomic positions until the convergence thresholds are met.
After the vc-relax completes, run a self-consistent field calculation on the fully relaxed structure using the same pseudopotentials, cutoffs, k-point grid, and convergence thresholds.
Return the fully relaxed structure (lattice vectors and atomic positions) and the final total energy from the SCF calculation.
Report all chosen numerical settings (ecutwfc, k-point mesh, spin treatment) along with the results.
